79f19e4a35de: Ask: «Which film is better — the last one you saw, or the one from last month?» Collect the answers and write 2–3 forms with mistakes on the board. We'll come back to them in the traps section.
cf56967be032: Three steps. Check with words: młody, nowy, zabawny. Stress that naj- is always written together.
d1b2d63cbcdc: Ask them to pronounce «łatwszy» — it is awkward. That is why -ejszy. The ł → l alternation in cieplejszy is the same as in the past tense.
7ca51f355b40: These forms are best learned in pairs. English does the same with short adjectives: high — higher, low — lower.
b29a0426da68: The rule: if the word is long or it is a participle (-ny, -ty, -ący) — use bardziej. You cannot combine bardziej with -szy.
6260b7c29d91: The degrees decline like an ordinary adjective. Watch the masculine personal form: lepsi, młodsi, wyżsi.
265d6315f0f4: Four forms that simply have to be memorised. Like English: good — better, bad — worse, much — more.
c40261789033: An adverb answers the question “how?”. English “faster” is both an adjective and an adverb; Polish distinguishes them.
73df3df7d398: Reveal row by row. Ask the student to make sentences about themselves: Oglądam więcej niż…, Śpię mniej niż…
2dd89492dfda: Two equally valid ways. Od + genitive, niż + the same case. English “than” can be rendered either way.
e68af2b09225: Typical mistake: «jeden z najlepszy serial». After jeden z always dopełniacz liczby mnogiej (genitive plural).
d2c71dc44057: The more I watch, the less I sleep.
08348cd04bd9: The longer the film, the more boring it is.
c0b5c99fe5ea: English “the more… the more…” → Polish im… tym. Do not use “czym” here.
5d81344ec7d9: TV series are getting longer and longer.
13389e6e4eff: This is a much better film.
bf48cd9a0b3a: Three useful constructions for conversation. Ask each student to say a sentence with coraz about their own life.
42a6e08b244f: The second trio — constructions. Ask the student to correct the mistakes from the warm-up.
